newsitem.title: USA: US oil majors may not meet output targets-analyst.
newsitem.headline: US oil majors may not meet output targets-analyst.

text.p: U.S. oil majors may find it difficult to meet their target of growing production this year by their target of 3.9 percent, Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting said.

He noted that a group of four majors, Amoco Corp, Exxon Corp, Occidental Petroleum Corp and Texaco Inc had reported a 0.6 percent decline in oil and natural gas liquids production in the first half of 1997 compared with the year-ago period.
"In order for the group to reach the 1997 versus 1996 target production growth rate of 3.98 percent, year over year oil and gas production growth in the second half would have to average 9.9 percent.

Ting said that Texaco should continue to show good production growth, but that Amoco is expected to review its production target at an analyst meeting in September and that Exxon has a reasonable chance of reaching its 4.7 percent target in the second half.
Occidental may have problems due to disruption at its Colombian operations due to attacks by leftist rebels on key oil infrastructure.
Ting said that slowing production by majors may not translate into a slowdown in global oil supply. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
